subject: Request: temporary on‑prem audit window + credit request (MediSync)
messages:
From: Amy Lee <amy.lee@medisync-health.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: audit@medisync-health.com
Date: 2026-12-01T09:12:00Z
Subject: Request: 48‑hour audit window at our DC + cost ask

Jonas —

Thanks again for the quick demo last week. Our compliance team needs a supervised, timeboxed access window to perform an on‑site audit of the tenant running in our VPC (private deployment). Scope: 48 hours of observer and runbook‑driven checks, one external auditor and two MediSync engineers on site.

We also want a credit because this deviates from your standard managed‑only policies; legal asked for a 25% one‑time service credit to cover the ops overhead. We attached the formal ask and a short checklist.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can: 
- Provide supervised SRE access to the hosted node for the 48‑hour window, 
- Keep a full stream of audit logs that we can retain, 
- Agree to no data export and no persistent shell access beyond jumpbox sessions.

Happy to jump on a call to walk through the checklist.

— Amy
Director, Compliance
MediSync Health

[Attachment: MediSync_audit_request.pdf (1 page)]

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Amy Lee <amy.lee@medisync-health.com>
Date: 2026-12-01T11:05:00Z
Subject: Fwd: Request: 48‑hour audit window at our DC + cost ask

Team — looping you in. MediSync (DL-2026-7832) has asked for a supervised 48‑hour on‑prem/VPC audit window and is requesting a 25% one‑time credit to offset our ops burden. This is non‑standard for Private deployments (we typically prohibit direct host access).

Key asks from customer: 
- Supervised SRE sessions via our jumpbox for two 48‑hour consecutive days; customer auditor will observe and run checks.
- Real‑time audit log export (read‑only) that MediSync can store; no data export allowed outside the window.
- KMS key not escrowed — customer will not request key material, but wants proof of KM operations audit.

Risks: host access increases blast radius and legal exposure, prep effort ~ 48–72 hours of infra & runbook work, we may need an amendment to MSA for indemnity and non‑exfiltration clauses.

Proposed deal team position for exec consideration: 
- Approve temporary supervised access for up to 72 hours prep + 48 hours window (total ops calendar impact).
- Approve a one‑time commercial concession of 15% credit (compromise).
- Require PS fee to cover runbook and on‑site coordination: $25k.
- Conditions: jumpbox only access, session recording retained, no key extraction, signed amendment prior to the window.

Please weigh in with approval or escalation. If we approve, I’ll prepare the amendment and a short internal ops checklist (attached).

— Jonas
Sr. AE, Redwood Inference

[Attachment: ops-checklist-jumpbox.txt]

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-01T15:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: 48‑hour audit window at our DC + cost ask

Jonas — thanks for the writeup. A few clarifying Qs before I sign off: 
1) Does MediSync want any KMS key material to be moved or escrowed? (per your note, sounds like no)
2) Which support tier is this customer on? If they’re Enterprise with current Dedicated support, we can be more flexible.
3) Who’s the legal owner for the amendment on their side (I need the contact so legal can loop in promptly).

If the ask is strictly observational with recorded sessions and a signoff amendment, I’m inclined to approve commercial compromise (15%) + PS fee. But need Dev to confirm operational feasibility and the minimum prep window.

— Lauren

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-02T09:40:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: 48‑hour audit window at our DC + cost ask

Quick operational note — we can support supervised jumpbox sessions and session recording, but we need: 
- 72 hours lead time to stage a dedicated temporary jumpbox and hardened ACLs, validate multi‑party session recording, and run a dry run.
- A signed amendment that explicitly forbids key extraction and describes permitted commands.
- A requirement that the customer’s auditor is observer‑only (no sudo).

Also: the 25% credit is steep given PS and scheduling impact. Suggest counter: 10% credit + mandatory $25k PS fee or waive credit if customer pays full PS. If sales needs better commercial we can land at 15% + $25k PS.

Operational impacts: 8 hours of SRE on‑call during the window, session storage retention for 90 days (we’ll produce a signed log export), and an ops runbook acceptance signoff.

— Dev
Principal Infra Engineer

> Team — looping you in. MediSync (DL-2026-7832) has asked for a supervised 48‑hour on‑prem/VPC audit window and is requesting a 25% one‑time credit to offset our ops burden. This is non‑standard for Private deployments (we typically prohibit direct host access).

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Amy Lee <amy.lee@medisync-health.com>
Date: 2026-12-03T16:40:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: 48‑hour audit window at our DC + cost ask — Exec decision

Jonas / team — reviewed. Approve with conditions. Final executive decision: 

1) Commercial: approve one‑time 15% credit applied to the next invoice AND require a $25,000 Professional Services fee to be invoiced upfront.
2) Operational window: customer picks a 48‑hour continuous window no earlier than 72 hours after signed amendment; ops prep takes up to 72 hours.
3) Security controls (mandatory):
   - Jumpbox access only (no direct host shells).
   - Session recording with redactible stream; logs retained for 90 days and shared read‑only.
   - Customer auditors are observer‑only (no sudo).
   - No KMS key material transfer or escrow; no data exfiltration allowed.
4) Legal: require a short MSA amendment capturing indemnity, non‑exfiltration covenant, scope and signoff. Legal to route the amendment to MediSync counsel and require countersignature before any access.
5) Escalation clause: if any session shows suspicious activity, Redwood reserves the right to terminate the session immediately and bill for incident response at standard PS rates.

Jonas — please send the amendment draft to Amy and loop Legal (cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.com). Ops, please schedule the dry run once amendment is signed. I’m fine with 15% + $25k PS given the exposure and precedent risk.

— Marissa
VP, Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: proposed-msa-amendment-v2.docx]
